# dsh-empty-turn-guard
**English** | 简体中文

A small DSH (DeepSeek-Harness) plugin for one
specific failure: the model replies with **nothing but

leaked protocol markup** —
no prose, no tool call — and the harness treats that as a finished turn.

This
plugin reclassifies it as a **retryable error** so the step is retried instead of
silently end

reclassifies it as a **retryable error** so the step is retried instead of
silently ending the turn.

It is a DSH **bundle** (a package with its own `cordis.patch.yml`) and installs
without touching any

H **bundle** (a package with its own `cordis.patch.yml`) and installs
without touching any DSH file.
## Features

- **Catches the "half an answer" turn.** When a reply ends with only
`</｜｜DSML｜｜ calls>`, `<thinking

> </thinking>`, or leftover punctuation, the
step is retried with backoff instead of being committed

as an answer.
- **Two settings entry points.** A dedicated tab under **Settings → Built-in
plugins

→ Empty-turn guard**, and the same card on the sidebar **Plugins**
panel. Both drive the same switch

.
- **Cannot false-positive on real replies.** Three conditions must hold at once:
the finish is `st

op`, no tool call was observed, and the text is empty after
markup removal. A one-word answer, a lon

e `?`, or prose that merely mentions a
tag passes through untouched.
- **Leaves truncation alone.**

`max-tokens` is a real answer cut short and already
surfaces as its own visible outcome, so it is no

t touched.
- **No dependencies at runtime.** Host half imports only a schema library; the
browser ha

lf is a hand-written bundle with no build step.
- **Logs the length, never the text.** Diagnostics c

arry `text=24ch`, so model
output does not reach log files through this plugin.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`dsh plugin … add` forwards its arguments to pnpm, so GitHub shorthands, tags and
branches work too
(`github:FYTXY/dsh-empty-turn-guard#v0.4.0`).

Restart DSH, then open **Settings → Built-in plugins → Empty-turn guard** and
turn the switch on.
Installing without the CLI

1. Put this directory somewhere stable, e.g. `~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-empty-turn-guard`.
2. Link it into

the profile's `node_modules` (symlink or Windows junction).
3. In the profile's `package.json`, add

the package name to **both**
`dependencies` and the `dsh.profile.bundles` array.
4. Restart DSH.

Do not insert a bare path row into `cordis.patch.yml` instead: that mounts the
plugin as a plain mod

ule rather than a bundle, and the settings card will not
appear.

With a `link:` or manual install, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` resolves from the
copy DSH already ship

s. If Node reports `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND:
@deepseek-ai/schemastery`, point at that copy:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A GitHub install handles this through pnpm and needs no extra step.
## Configuration
### 1. The switch

Both entry points write the same value — the package's entry in the profile's
`dsh.profile.bundles`
array — so either works:
| Entry point | What it shows |
| Settings → Built-in plugins → **Empty-turn guard** | The plugin's own tab: the switch, what it cur

rently does, and save / discard |
| Sidebar → **Plugins** panel | The same switch on the bundle's ca

ly does, and save / discard |
| Sidebar → **Plugins** panel | The same switch on the bundle's card |

Turning it **off** unloads the plugin and restores the untouched `llm/stream`
chain, which brings th

e silent half-turn back. Turning it **on** reloads the
guard. Both take effect without reinstalling.

The row-level toggle for this plugin's row is greyed out on the Plugins panel.
That is expected: DSH

only enables or disables *rows* through the profile's own
patch file, and this plugin's row comes f

rom the bundle's own `cordis.patch.yml`.
The bundle switch is the one that takes effect.
### 2. Disabling it without unloading
To keep the package installed but skip the interception, give the row a config:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`enabled` is a volatile field, so it arrives as a live reference rather than a
frozen value; the gua

rd re-reads it on every request and the settings switch
applies to the next model call with no resta

re-reads it on every request and the settings switch
applies to the next model call with no restart.
### 3. Verifying it is running

In the host log (`%APPDATA%\DSH Desktop\logs\host\dsh-<date>.log` on Windows,
`~/.config/DSH Desktop
/logs/host/` on Linux):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
And when a markup-only stop is actually caught:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

An `llm/retry` / `llm/retry-started` event usually follows — that is the retry
running.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`llm/stream` is the single funnel every model call passes through, and the
waterfall lets a listener

wrap the provider's chunk stream instead of reacting
after the fact. Rewriting the `finish` chunk —

rather than editing text or
injecting a message — keeps the conversation history clean and reuses t

he retry
machinery the provider already declares.

Two filters keep the interception narrow. Requests that declare no tools are
skipped, because backgr

ound calls (session titles, compaction) stream the same
way and an empty reply there is expected. `m

ax-tokens` is skipped because a
truncated answer is a genuine answer.

The failure this targets, the measurements behind it, and why switching protocol
does not help are d
ocumented in **docs/root-cause.md**.
## Compatibility

- **DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`** (verified on this release).
- **Node.js >= 22.**
- Uses only existing seams:

the `llm/stream` waterfall and the `EMPTY_RESPONSE`
error code. No DSH file is modified.
- `@deepsee

k-ai/schemastery` is a **peer dependency** supplied by DSH.
- The schema keeps a `.volatile()` field

on purpose. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-settings`
drops any namespace whose schema has none — silently — and

the settings card
would vanish. See the note at the end of
docs/root-cause.md.
## Non-goals

- **Does not repair the relay.** The markup still reaches the message body; it
just no longer preten

ds to be a finished turn.
